summary:
R4 is the model to lean on today — 62% at +18.0u over the last 14 days (47-29) and +11.0u over the last 7 (21-13, 62%), the best short-window unit return of any rating despite the smallest sample. Bullpen category is the engine behind it, hot everywhere: R1/R2/R3 all sit at 53% with 3W streaks, and R4's bullpen number is running even hotter at 58% (110-79) over the last 14. Contrast that with hitting, which is ice cold across the board — R1 45%, R3 46% with a 4L streak, R4 49% with a 5L streak — so any pick leaning on hitting-driven edges today should get discounted, and bullpen_fatigue remains a fade at 44% across all four ratings.

On today's board, all four ratings line up in full consensus on nine of fifteen games, and the CIN @ MIL top play is the one to trust most: MIL graded +3.34 to +4.34 across every rating, and MIL as a picked team is 37-21 (64%) on the season with a strong-play mark of 22-12 (+10.0u) — exactly the profile bullpen strength and trends+sp combos (56.8% hit, the best category pair) tend to reward. TEX @ ARI is the second-strongest consensus (+2.31 to +2.87) and worth similar confidence. The LAD @ MIA line is the sharpest fade of the day — all four ratings favor LAD by -1.57 to -1.90, but that's backwards; LAD is 31-13 (70%) when picked with a stellar 23-4 (85%, +25.0u) strong-play record, so this negative delta reads as fading LAD, which conflicts with the season data and deserves a second look before trusting blindly. BOS's KCR matchup is a smaller lean (-0.35 to -0.87) but BOS as a picked team is the best team play on the board at 72% (39-15) with a 76% strong-play hit rate, so lean into anything pushing toward Boston even on modest deltas. NYY @ NYM is a clean, low-variance nine-way consensus around +0.90 to +1.27 backed by ace Gerrit Cole, while the two SPLIT games — LAA/WSN and SDP/SFG — carry deltas so thin (sub-0.15 on the dissenting side) they're essentially coin flips and shouldn't be strong plays regardless of side.
